# Calibration simulation (generated by calibration_sim.ts)

3000 virtual users per stated skin type, 30 outings each, next-morning report after each. UV error per outing from the measured band (satellite, 2 h: log-SD 0.19). Seeded, reproducible.

- **error**: median factor between estimated and true MED (10% = typically off by ×1.10).
- **over-trust**: estimated MED > 1.25 × true, i.e. the app thinks you have 25%+ more time than you do.
- **pink at 100%**: if you leave exactly when the app says 100%, how often the real dose still reaches your real MED. "central" = the single estimate; "cautious" = what the Bayesian alerts use (UV and skin uncertainty combined).
- **80% interval**: how often the true MED is inside the posterior 10th–90th percentile (should be ~80%).

## Sensitivity: report-noise settings (after 30 check-ins, averaged over types I–VI)

| world | likelihood settings (report σ / sunscreen σ / random answers) | error | over-trust | pink at cautious 100% | 80% interval holds truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| as assumed | shipped (0.30 / 0.50 / 5%) | 9% | 3% | 12% | 80% |
| as assumed | robust (0.45 / 0.70 / 10%) | 11% | 13% | 19% | 82% |
| harsher | shipped (0.30 / 0.50 / 5%) | 16% | 3% | 7% | 59% |
| harsher | robust (0.45 / 0.70 / 10%) | 13% | 8% | 12% | 78% |

Shipped settings are kept: if the assumptions hold, robust settings under-react to real redness (over-trust and cautious-pink rise). If reality is harsher, shipped settings give too-narrow intervals but err on the safe side.


## Limits

- Simulated people, not real ones. The "harsher" world shows what happens if the assumptions are wrong; it is not data.
- Real check-in answers may be biased (people forget, or under-report mild pink), which no world here models.
- Types V–VI rarely reach a burn dose, so most reports are "none" and learning is slow by nature.
